source_basis: ConceptCoder section2.1 definition adapted to testing; no training/bottleneck reproduction

cards.scope: named text value before and after one transformation
cards.observation: Record the actual transform and whether it changes the bound value on this input; reaching the call is insufficient.
cards.requirement: Record which textual distinctions the public specification requires preserving; if case policy is unstated or conflicting, retain unknown.
cards.obligation: Find two admissible values whose required distinction is collapsed by the bound transform, and confirm the changed value reaches the named downstream observation.
cards.benign: Case-insensitive comparison explicitly permits lower/casefold; an alphabet without case variation cannot exercise this case.
cards.compact: lower collapses A/a here. If this output must preserve case, exercise a case-only contrast; expected output comes from the spec/oracle.
cards.guide: Preserve original data for case-sensitive comparisons; normalize only where the contract permits it.
cards.unknown_rule: Missing evidence stays unknown; unknown is not false and is not covered.
cards.coverage_rule: Record site reachability separately; mark an obligation exercised only when its named semantic predicate is observed on an admissible test. This does not establish oracle correctness or absence of bugs.
cards.pipeline_connection: candidate only: extract OBS and REQ separately, then bind a specific TEST obligation; no arbitrary same-line fact may stand in for it

cards.scope: a bound collection and its consumer
cards.observation: Identify whether a specific projection collapses repetitions and whether its consumer observes counts or only membership.
cards.requirement: Determine whether the named result depends on occurrence counts or only distinct membership; do not infer this from set syntax.
cards.obligation: Exercise equal-support collections with different multiplicities and establish the bound projection collapses that distinction. Output invariance is a bug hypothesis only if the required output depends on multiplicity.
cards.benign: Distinct-element count and membership queries intentionally discard duplicate occurrences.

example.contract: Return the number of occurrences in the list.

cards.compact: set collapses [2,2,7] and [2,7]. If the requested quantity counts occurrences, use this contrast; distinct-member tasks are benign.
cards.guide: Use occurrence counts when requested; retain set-based logic for explicitly distinct-member semantics.
cards.unknown_rule: Missing evidence stays unknown; unknown is not false and is not covered.

cards.scope: one comparison between two bound values
cards.observation: Determine which order the expression implements from operand types/operator; require a pair for which implemented and required order disagree.
cards.requirement: Ground numeric magnitude or the external ranking in an explicit public specification; never obtain the order from the grading reference.
cards.obligation: Exercise an admissible inversion pair at the bound comparator and check that the comparison influences the named result.
cards.benign: Dictionary-order tasks intentionally use lexical comparison; distinct orders can also agree on an individual pair.

example.contract: Select the string representing the larger integer.

cards.compact: String order ranks "10" before "2"; numeric order reverses it. Exercise an inversion only if this comparison requires numeric rank.
cards.guide: Compare the contract-specified key or rank; retain original values for the requested output.

cards.observation: Read the explicit literal table and observe membership for a bound symbol; independently record the required classifier from public spec/examples.
cards.requirement: Spell out allowed alphabet and required class; "case sensitive" alone does not establish lower-only vowel membership.
cards.obligation: Exercise a legal symbol in the symmetric difference of observed and required finite classes at an eligible consumer position. Record whether downstream eligibility conditions hold.
cards.benign: A lower-only table is valid when the input contract guarantees lowercase or normalization precedes the lookup.

example.contract: Both uppercase and lowercase A/E/I/O/U are vowels; return the matching original character between consonants.

cards.compact: The table contains lowercase vowels only. For a contract admitting uppercase vowels, exercise an eligible uppercase vowel; preserve its case in the expected result.
cards.guide: Use the contract-complete classifier or normalize only for membership while retaining the original character if required.

cards.scope: recursive call graph or a bounded execution trace
cards.observation: Separate argument progress, base-case coverage, recursion depth and repeated work. Different properties require different measurements; repeated identical subproblem arguments are not proved by visiting a recursive call line.
cards.requirement: Resource failures require a declared admissible input range and evaluation resource budget. Without them, retain a performance hypothesis, not a confirmed correctness bug.
cards.obligation: Under a declared budget, show repeated unshared subproblems or depth growth on admissible inputs. Do not generate enormous expected integers or declare nontermination from recursion syntax.
cards.benign: Small bounded input domains can permit naive recursion; memoization may share repeated subproblem requests even when the source has multiple recursive calls.
cards.compact: Progress and duplicated recursive work are separate. Measure overlap/reuse under the declared input and resource budget; reaching recursion is not coverage.
cards.guide: Share repeated subproblems or use an iterative recurrence when the declared resource contract requires it.
